# token-budget

> Context-management infrastructure for long-running AI agents: keeps
> a growing conversation (messages, tool calls, tool results) inside a
> token budget via pluggable eviction/summarization strategies, atomic
> tool-call/tool-result preservation, pinned instructions, oversized
> tool-output truncation, and an explainable decision trace. Not a
> tokenizer, not an agent framework — a layer underneath whatever's
> already orchestrating your agent (a raw provider SDK, LangChain.js,
> or the Vercel AI SDK).

This file is a navigation pointer to the canonical documentation below,
nothing more — it makes no claims about search ranking or AI citation.

## Start here

- [README](https://github.com/shivam039/token-budget/blob/main/README.md) — positioning, install, the smallest example, the `getContext()`/`commit()` lifecycle
- [FAQ](https://github.com/shivam039/token-budget/blob/main/docs/FAQ.md) — direct answers: what a context window is, how to trim history, how to preserve tool calls, which integrations exist
- [AI agent context management guide](https://github.com/shivam039/token-budget/blob/main/docs/guides/ai-agent-context-management.md) — the full shape of the problem and how each piece is addressed
- [Tool-output context management guide](https://github.com/shivam039/token-budget/blob/main/docs/guides/tool-output-context-management.md) — preventing one oversized tool result from consuming the budget

## Try it

- [Coding-agent example](https://github.com/shivam039/token-budget/tree/main/examples/coding-agent-context) — realistic, deterministic, runnable in under a minute, no API key required
- [Cookbook](https://github.com/shivam039/token-budget/blob/main/packages/token-budget/COOKBOOK.md) — four tested recipes (customer support, coding agent, RAG chat, long-form writing)
